Recurrence counts only at population-hotspot scale (cancerhotspots.org thresholds; COSMIC or a tumour-type-specific study only for tumour types those resources cover poorly), so a handful of cases in one cohort does not qualify. Without functional data, a non-hotspot missense change usually reaches only OM1/OP1/OP4-level points and stays a VUS. OncoKB keeps 'oncogenic' separate from the biological effect (gain-of-function = activating). It gives hotspots based only on statistical recurrence 'Likely Oncogenic', and functional characterisation overrides recurrence. question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: Under standard somatic-variant interpretation guidelines (AMP/ASCO/CAP, ClinGen/CGC/VICC oncogenicity SOP), what evidence is needed to call a non-hotspot kinase missense variant 'activating', and can genomic patterns alone (mutual exclusivity, recurrence) meet it? ANSWER: Under the ClinGen/CGC/VICC SOP (Horak et al. 2022), oncogenicity is scored by adding up listed evidence codes. OS2 is well-established in vitro/in vivo functional studies (4 points). OS1 is the same amino acid change as an established oncogenic variant (4). OS3 is a cancerhotspots.org hotspot with at least 50 samples at the position and at least 10 with the same change (4). OM1 is a critical, well-established functional-domain site (2). OM3 is a smaller hotspot (2). OM4 is a different oncogenic missense change at the same residue (2). OP1 is in-silico predictions that all agree (1). OP3 is a hotspot where the same change is seen fewer than 10 times (1). OP4 is absence from gnomAD (1). 'Likely oncogenic' needs at least 6 points and 'oncogenic' at least 10. AMP/ASCO/CAP lists data types but gives no oncogenicity rules; the Horak SOP was written to fill that gap. Mutual exclusivity and co-mutation patterns are not criteria in the SOP. Recurrence counts only at population-hotspot scale (cancerhotspots.org thresholds; COSMIC or a tumour-type-specific study only for tumour types those resources cover poorly), so a handful of cases in one cohort does not qualify. Without functional data, a non-hotspot missense change usually reaches only OM1/OP1/OP4-level points and stays a VUS. OncoKB keeps 'oncogenic' separate from the biological effect (gain-of-function = activating). It gives hotspots based only on statistical recurrence 'Likely Oncogenic', and functional characterisation overrides recurrence. Conclusion: genotype and co-mutation tables alone cannot establish activation, and they cannot refute it either; that needs a functional or pathway readout (e.g., MAPK/ERK phosphorylation, kinase assay, transformation assay). HOW SURE: high. question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: Is there any validated method to infer small cell lung cancer transcriptional subtypes (ASCL1/NEUROD1/POU2F3/YAP1-defined) from DNA-only data, such as targeted-panel mutations or copy number, without RNA or IHC? ANSWER: Not from mutations or copy number. A 2024 review states that no broad SCLC subtypes have been identified from mutational profiles and that mutation-based cfDNA profiling has not proved useful for subtyping. The only validated DNA-based approach is DNA methylation (tumour or cfDNA methylome classifiers, e.g. Heeke et al., Cancer Cell 2024). Panel mutation/CNA/SV/segment tables hold no methylation data, so they hold no recognised subtype proxy. HOW SURE: high. SOURCES: https://www.cell.com/trends/molecular-medicine/fulltext/S1471-4914(24)00218-1, https://www.cell.com/cancer-cell/fulltext/S1535-6108(24)00006-0.

question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: In public cancer-genomics portals, how are circulating-tumour-cell-derived xenografts (CDX) usually encoded in sample-class fields? Are they typically lumped under 'PDX'/'xenograft'? ANSWER: Yes, in cBioPortal. Its datahub curation rules allow SAMPLE_CLASS only the values 'Tumor', 'Cell Line' or 'Xenograft', so there is no CDX category and CTC-derived xenografts fall under Xenograft/PDX-type classes. They can be told apart only through other fields (e.g. specimen source = blood/CTC, or the sample ID). In SCLC literature, CDX means CTC-derived xenograft, a patient-derived model alongside tissue PDX. Elsewhere, CDX often means cell line-derived xenograft. I found no portal-wide rule beyond cBioPortal's, so how a given study fills its own free-text class field is not settled by the web. HOW SURE: medium. SOURCES: https://github.com/cBioPortal/datahub/blob/master/docs/curation-process.md, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5583071/, https://www.fredhutch.org/content/dam/www/shared-resources/PMCL/FAQ-PM-CDX-PDX.pdf.

question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: How is chromoplexy operationally defined and detected in whole-genome sequencing studies? What minimum data (junction coordinates, orientations, copy-number breakpoints) do chain-detection algorithms need, and can it be inferred from copy-number segments alone? ANSWER: Baca et al. 2013 (Cell) define chromoplexy as chains of interdependent rearrangements (translocations and deletions). In these chains, breakpoints from different rearrangements lie near each other on the reference genome, often joined by deletions at the fusion junctions ('deletion bridges'). The chains are closed and cause little or no copy-number change (Genes Dev 2013 review). ChainFinder, the detection tool from the original study, builds a graph: rearrangement breakpoints from WGS junction calls are the nodes, and chromosomal deletion segments from copy-number data are the edges. It then finds sets of connected breakpoints that are statistically unlikely to have arisen independently. Junction-level calls (breakpoint coordinates on both sides, with orientation) are therefore the required input. Copy-number deletion segments are only a supplementary input that links breakpoints into chains. Later measures (OAR and copy-number asymmetry enrichment, BMC Genomics 2014; JaBbA junction-graph classification, 2019 preprint) also use adjacencies/junctions, combined with copy number. None of the pages read describes detecting chromoplexy from copy-number segments alone. Because chromoplexy is largely copy-neutral, CN segments by themselves cannot show it. At most they can show deletions and breakpoints that fit with it. That last point is my inference from the definition, not a statement any source makes. HOW SURE: high for the definition and ChainFinder inputs; medium for 'cannot be inferred from CN alone' (inferred, not stated explicitly). SOURCES: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3690918/, https://www.genome.gov/Multimedia/Slides/HGP10Symposium/11_Garraway.pdf, https://genesdev.cshlp.org/content/27/23/2513.long, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/1471-2164-15-S6-S4, https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/836296v1.full.

question: FINDING FROM THE LAB'S LIBRARY, asked for by the director. QUESTION: In prostate cancer FISH assays for ERG rearrangement, what do the categories 'translocation' and 'translocation with deletion' (interstitial deletion) indicate about how the fusion formed? ANSWER: TMPRSS2 and ERG lie about 3 Mb apart on chromosome 21q22, in the same orientation. The fusion therefore forms in one of two ways, which ERG break-apart FISH can tell apart. (1) 'Translocation' (split signal, Esplit, 'rearrangement through insertion'): the 5' and 3' ERG probe signals separate but both are kept. The intervening DNA was moved elsewhere without loss, as in a balanced translocation or insertion. (2) 'Translocation with deletion' (interstitial deletion, Edel): the 5' ERG signal is lost. The roughly 3 Mb of DNA between TMPRSS2 and ERG (21q22.2-3) was deleted, which joins the two genes directly. SNP arrays show a recurrent deletion with two start-point subclasses. Edel makes up roughly half to 60% of fusion-positive primary tumours and is linked to higher stage, nodal metastasis and androgen-independent disease. These categories describe how each fusion formed. They do not by themselves show whether a rearrangement belongs to a multi-partner chromoplexy chain. Baca et al. report that 15 of 26 TMPRSS2-ERG fusions in their WGS cohort arose within chromoplexy chains (Garraway slides), but FISH cannot show this. HOW SURE: high. SOURCES: https://aacrjournals.org/cancerres/article/66/17/8337/526226/TMPRSS2-ERG-Fusion-Associated-Deletions-Provide, https://www.modernpathology.org/article/S0893-3952(22)02665-5/fulltext, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2760294/, https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC1601467/, https://www.genome.gov/Multimedia/Slides/HGP10Symposium/11_Garraway.pdf.

Excluding the rectum, the transverse colon, or both leaves every gene right-enriched (see the location reply), so the result does not depend on the sidedness convention.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (SV/G659): In the MSS one-sample-per-patient set (174 Right, 488 Left), data_sv.txt adds 2 BRAF in-frame fusions (both Right), 1 RNF43 fusion (Left) and 2 SMAD4 SVs (both Left). None of the 15 RNF43 truncating calls (10 Right, 5 Left) is G659fs, so excluding it changes nothing. With SVs added, RNF43 is 5.7% vs 1.2% (p=0.002) and SMAD4 is 21.8% vs 17.2% (p=0.21). Under the stricter OncoKB SMAD4 definition (truncating, deep deletion and curated MH2 missense only) plus SVs, SMAD4 is 15.5% vs 10.7% (p=0.10). Direction is unchanged and the label stays True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (sample type): In the MSS analysis set, metastasis samples make up 221/488 (45%) of Left and 67/174 (39%) of Right (Fisher p=0.13). CMH tests stratified by SAMPLE_TYPE leave every gene's direction unchanged: KRAS OR 2.87 (p=3e-9), BRAF 3.28 (p=1e-5), PIK3CA 1.99 (p=0.002), AKT1 (p=0.025), RNF43 4.73 (p=0.001), SMAD4 1.56 (p=0.076). The six-gene set gives OR 6.3. Stratification does not change the method or the label.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (MCRC_TYPE): There are 123 Early Stage Primary samples in the whole cohort, but only 45 (31 Left, 14 Right) are in the MSS one-sample-per-patient set. Excluding them (160 Right, 457 Left) gives the same results: KRAS p=1e-8, BRAF p=5e-5, PIK3CA p=0.007, RNF43 p=0.002, AKT1 p=0.067, SMAD4 16.3% vs 10.9% (p=0.09), and the six-gene set OR 7.0 (p=3e-18). A CMH test by MCRC_TYPE is also unchanged. The label is unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 (decision rule): The rule, written before rerunning, was that the claim is supported if the set-level test (any oncogenic alteration in the six genes, Right vs Left) is significant with Right higher and no gene is significantly enriched on the Left. The set-level result is 86% vs 49% (OR 6.4, p=1e-18). Without KRAS it is 48% vs 26% (OR 2.65, p=1.4e-7). All six genes point Right; four are individually significant, while AKT1 (2 vs 0) and SMAD4 (p=0.10) are underpowered. Under the rule the label is True, and it does not depend on SMAD4 reaching significance alone.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (gene universe): Under the length-weighted per-sample null for the 20-gene curated ERBB-PI3K set, an exome-wide universe (1.07e7 aa, about 19000 genes) gives 5/56 hit vs 2.66 expected, p=0.12 (p=0.064 without hypermutator NPC15F). Restricting the universe to the 1332-1412 genes present in the MAF raises the pathway fraction about 13-fold (expected about 21) and gives p=1. That universe conditions on the outcome and is wrong. The exome-wide universe is correct and is also the most liberal choice, so the universe choice does not by itself make the pathway significant. An unweighted gene-count null gives p=0.013, so gene length (the pathway genes are long, about 1150 aa on average) is what keeps the curated test non-significant.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (hypermutator): NPC15F has 332 of 1481 filtered nonsilent mutations and 0 hits in the ERBB-PI3K genes (curated or KEGG). In a per-sample null it adds about 0.5 expected hit-samples that are not observed, so including it is conservative: curated p=0.12 with it, 0.064 without it; curated+RAS p=0.014 with it, 0.006 without it. A per-sample null already handles hypermutators, so the full cohort stays primary, with the exclusion reported as a sensitivity check. This direction alone does not flip the call.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (RAS and hotspots): The MAF Hotspot column is 0 for every call and so carries no information. Still, the observed pathway hits include three canonical activating hotspots: PIK3CA E545K (NPC14F), KRAS G12V (NPC3D) and NRAS Q61R (NPC10F). Adding only HRAS/KRAS/NRAS (567 aa) to the 20-gene curated set gives 7/56 samples hit vs 2.72 expected, length-weighted per-sample null p=0.014 (0.006 without NPC15F). RAS directly activates PI3K downstream of ERBB receptors, and MSigDB KEGG_MEDICUS RTK_RAS_PI3K includes HRAS/KRAS/NRAS. Three canonical hotspots among 1481 mutations is far above chance (expected about 0.003 if about 20 canonical hotspot residues are spread over the proteome). This changed the call from True to False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 hotspots: PIK3CA E545K, KRAS G12V and NRAS Q61R each occur once in 56 NPC samples, and the MAF Hotspot column is 0 for all 1575 calls. Single known hotspots show that drivers are present but do not test whether the pathway is significantly mutated. Changes method: yes, hotspots are now descriptive only.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 filtering: the NPC MAF has 68 FILTER=common_variant calls and 17 with ExAC AF>1%. None of the 8 ERBB-PI3K pathway hits are among them (all have AF absent or <0.001). After filtering, 1482 nonsynonymous calls remain (missense, nonsense, splice, frameshift, in-frame del, nonstop, start). The filter changes the background slightly, not the pathway hits; I adopted it.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 gene length: the 25 ERBB-PI3K pathway genes average about 1013 aa against about 560 aa genome-wide, so an unweighted random-gene-set null underestimates the expected hits. With a length-weighted, per-sample-count null, the broad set gives 7 samples hit vs 3.0-3.7 expected (p=0.02-0.06), and the earlier unweighted p=0.006 was inflated. Changes method: yes.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 RAS genes: under the length-weighted null, the narrow ERBB+PI3K/PTEN/AKT set gives 4/56 samples hit vs 1.5-1.8 expected (p=0.05-0.10); adding mTOR/TSC gives p=0.05-0.10; the broad set without RAS gives p=0.16-0.28. Only the broad set with KRAS/NRAS gives p about 0.02. Earlier I ran about 3 null/universe variants and reported the most significant one. Changes the call from False to True (not significantly mutated, borderline).

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (per-patient counts, P-0048073, mutations only): Per-patient acquired counts (mut/CNA/SV) are FN 13120 0/13/0, 18770 2/3/0, 35844 6/8/2 over 2 pairs, 48073 2/17/1, 50430 2/0/0, 51132 6/6/0, 51453 1/0/0, 73133 1/2/0, 74869 1/5/0, 77663 0/0/0; FP 6113 0/1/0, 19531 1/1/0, 22317 0, 28971 0, 33453 1/0/1, 45478 0/2/0, 60318 0/2/2, 63459 1/0/0, 68164 0, 69477 3/0/0. All: FN mean 7.8 vs FP 1.5, MWU p=0.022. Without P-0048073: 6.4 vs 1.5, p=0.039. Mutations only: 2.1 vs 0.6, p=0.047 (2.1 vs 0.6, p=0.07 without P-0048073). Same-panel subset has 6 FN and 7 FP patients: 4.7 vs 1.4, p=0.15. The direction never changes, so the method stands.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (below-threshold events): Using hg19 gene positions in data_cna_hg19.seg, I flagged acquired CNAs where the earliest sample's seg.mean was already beyond 0.2 in the same direction. That was 32 of 54 FN CNAs (mostly P-0048073 chr17 and P-0013120 chr16) and 4 of 6 FP CNAs, or 39% of all acquired events. data_cna.txt has only 0/±2, so there are no ±1 calls to check. data_mutations.txt holds only 78 called somatic rows with no fill-out rows in earlier samples, so t_alt_count in the earlier sample cannot be checked for any acquired mutation. With the flagged CNAs removed, FN is 4.6 vs FP 1.1 acquired per patient, MWU p=0.045. The direction is unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (no shared mutations reading): Mutations shared between a patient's paired samples are not zero in FN-RMS: 6 of 10 FN patients share at least one, including P-0074869 6 (TP53, BCOR, SUFU...), P-0077663 3 (HRAS, CTNNB1, WT1), P-0073133 2 (DICER1), P-0051453 NRAS, P-0050430 TP53 and P-0018770 PAX5. Only 5 of 10 FP patients share one. Under this reading the 'no common mutations' clause is also contradicted. Under the patient-level reading, MDM2 amplification, BAP1 deep loss and TP53 mutation are each acquired in 2 FN patients. The verdict stays False.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 (ordering and lost events): My analysis already ordered samples Primary first, then by AGE_AT_SEQ_REPORTED_YEARS (almost all 18, so it does not separate them), then by T-number. So P-0045478, P-0068164, P-0074869 and P-0077663 already use the Primary (higher T-number) as the baseline, and the counts do not change. Lost events: FN 3.2 vs FP 1.2 per patient (p=0.034), so FN is more discordant in both directions. Acquired exceeds lost in FN (7.8 vs 3.2, net +4.6) but not in FP (1.5 vs 1.2, net +0.3). No check gives FN fewer acquired events than FP. Label stays False, though part of the FN excess may be heterogeneity or noise.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (collapsed vs full IPI): Against the full 0-5 IPI score on 618 patients with 185 deaths, the genomic PROGNOSTIC_MODEL has a lower Harrell C (0.673 vs 0.682; bootstrap delta C median -0.009, 95% CI -0.056 to 0.037) but a much better Cox fit (partial AIC 2085 linear or 2082 categorical vs 2119 linear or 2124 categorical IPI; delta AIC median 33, positive in 92% of 300 bootstraps). The three-group IPI is only a sensitivity check. The label does not rest on it, but discrimination against the full score is a tie, not a win.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (PH): The Schoenfeld rank test shows the PH assumption is violated for both the genomic model (p=0.012) and full IPI (p=0.045), so AIC does not favour one model unfairly. Time-specific cumulative AUCs are mixed: IPI is better at 12, 24 and 36 months (0.70/0.71/0.735 vs 0.65/0.68/0.70) and the genomic model is better at 60 months (0.708 vs 0.696). The genomic model's advantage is in long-term risk separation and the size of the extreme groups, not in early discrimination. This lowers the weight I give AIC alone.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (IPI missingness/factors): IPI is missing for 42% of patients without a genomic label vs 16%, 17% and 20% in the low, medium and high genomic groups. The IPI column equals the sum of its five factors in all 761 patients where all are present. Among labelled patients with no IPI (n=135), the genomic model's C is 0.61. The paired complete-case set (n=618) stays valid for a head-to-head comparison, and the method and patient set are unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 (definition of outperform): I define 'outperform' as a better likelihood-based fit (AIC, non-nested) together with discrimination that is no worse, following the library finding that AIC/LR is the primary evidence and delta C is low-power. The genomic model meets this in-sample: delta AIC about 34 for 2 vs 1 or 5 parameters, which is far larger than the parameter penalty, while C is tied. Its labels were derived on this cohort, so optimism cannot be corrected from the data, and a CV mutation-only model reached only C=0.52. I keep True, with low-to-moderate confidence.

Under the strict definition there are 0 NFKBIE promoter mutations in 20 DM. My earlier 'promoter' call was wrong and the label changes from False to True.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (ENST00000477930): all_effects gives no DISTANCE, BIOTYPE or TSL for ENST00000477930, only 'upstream_gene_variant'. The same isoform gives p.Gly75Glu for the Au2 variant at chr6:44233109, so its start lies downstream of 44233400 inside the canonical coding exon. The upstream label only means the variant is 5' of this alternative isoform's start; on the canonical transcript the variant is coding (CDS 101/1503). It is not a promoter mutation. This changes the method.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY library finding (VEP upstream_gene_variant): Checked against the data, the finding holds. The NFKBIE variants are upstream of non-canonical ENST00000477930 but missense in the coding exon of canonical ENST00000275015. So the upstream label is not evidence of a promoter location.

label: REPLY
text: Q1 purity/site: hg19 seg at ERBB2 (chr17:37.86-37.88Mb) confirms both candidate losses. P-0000444 post (GEJ primary) is flat chr17 at 0.10 but FGA 0.11, median VAF 0.12 (~24% purity) and a different site from the pre-TX liver met, so it is indeterminate. YJ-her-010 post (same cardia site) has FGA 0.59, median VAF 0.40 (~80% purity), segment 0.23 vs pre 2.47, a robust loss of ERBB2 amplification. One robust loss remains, so the label holds but the evidence is thinner.

label: REPLY
text: Q2 acquired-resistance subset: every HER2-amplified pair has HER2_TX_STATUS OFF TREATMENT. Best response is POD only for YJ-her-005, -012, -013, and all three kept ERBB2 amp post-TX. Both losses are non-POD: P-0000444 CR, TTP 25.4 mo; YJ-her-010 SD, TTP 7.6 mo. On the acquired-resistance subset (~19 pairs) the count of losses is unchanged at 2 (1 robust). The label does not change.

label: REPLY
text: Q3 association test: among 1st-line HER2 cohort samples with TTP (n=60), HER2_IMPACT LR correlates with TTP (Spearman rho 0.42, p=0.0008). Among AMP pre-TX samples only (n=56), rho is 0.32, p=0.017. HER2_IMPACT non-amplified (IHC/FISH+) cases have shorter TTP (median 5.8 vs 12.9 mo, MWU p=0.007) and none reached CR/PR (0/4 vs 38/56). IHC/FISH-negative-but-IMPACT-AMP discordance shows no TTP difference (p=0.63). A larger non-amplified/lower-amplitude component goes with worse trastuzumab outcome, which agrees with the case-level reading. The method is unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: Q4 control: none of the PRE/POST pairs without trastuzumab (P-0000797, -1047, -1551, -1699, FOLFOX) were ERBB2-amplified pre-TX, so the data give no background rate of amp loss. YJ-her-006/-014 (text 'mDCF') kept amp. Fisher 2/22 vs 0/4 gives p=1.0, uninformative. Without a control, a statistical association cannot be formally shown. I keep False on the direct evidence of a high-purity, same-site loss at progression plus the Q3 outcome association, with lower confidence.

label: REPLY
text: Q1 panel check: all 69 samples are MSK-IMPACT (341:3, 410:21, 468:45); data_cna.txt has 1677 gene rows (union of panels) and contains YAP1, MYCL, NKX2-1 but not ASCL1, NEUROD1 or POU2F3; mutations file (223 genes) has none of them. So these genes are not measured on any panel version ('not on panel', not 'no alteration'), and anyway subtypes are defined by expression, not DNA alteration; label stays Not verifiable.

label: REPLY
text: Q2 absence claim: no data on presence is not evidence of absence, since subtypes are defined by RNA/IHC expression which is not measured here. CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED has only histology (SCLC 63, combined SCLC 4, LCNEC 1, LNET 1), GRADE only grade, and the YAP1 CNA row (0:66, -1:2, +2:1) is copy number, not expression; library finding confirms no validated DNA-panel subtype proxy. Label stays Not verifiable.

label: REPLY
text: Q3 CDX: 42 PDX samples by PROCEDURE_TYPE: Biopsy 12, Autopsy 9, Blood Draw 8 (tissue site blood), Surgical 7, Aspiration 3, Pleural Effusion 3; the 8 blood-draw PDX are best read as CTC-derived xenografts (CDX). In-scope set is all 42 PDX/CDX models, but no file has subtype/expression variables for any of them, so scope does not change the Not verifiable label.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (germline/artefact): For the NFKBIE calls at chr6:44233400 (12M, 35M, Au3, Au7), 44233401 (12M) and 44233439 (Au3), t/n_alt_count and t/n_ref_count are all '.', Mutation_Status and SOMATIC are empty, and dbSNP_RS, GMAF and ExAC_AF are empty. Hotspot is 0 and FILTER is '.'. 44233400 and 44233401 are both in 12M, so that is a CC>TT dinucleotide (UV signature) split into two SNPs. All samples have matched normals. The exact position recurs in 4 independent tumours and is absent from dbSNP/ExAC, which argues against germline. Artefact cannot be ruled out without read counts. Method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (strict vs broad): Canonical ENST00000275015 (NM_004556.2) has CDS 1503 bp with CDS_position equal to cDNA_position (c.101 = cDNA 101/2556), so it has no annotated 5'UTR and its TSS is about chr6:44233500 (minus strand). No NFKBIE-window row lies above 44233500 apart from TMEM151B 44244198, so the STRICT reading (non-coding, upstream of the canonical TSS) gives 0/20 (Pure 0/13, Mixed 0/7) and the label True. The BROAD reading (5'-end hotspot ~100 bp downstream of the TSS, which VEP calls upstream_gene_variant of NFKBIE isoform ENST00000477930) gives 4/20 samples at 44233400 (Pure 3/13: 12M, Au3, Au7; Mixed 1/7: 35M) and the label False. I chose broad because the first AUG of the 500-aa ORF is not used in vivo (the next REPLY explains why), so codon 34 is effectively untranslated 5' sequence next to the TSS, not real coding sequence.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (transcripts): all_effects for 44233400/401/439 lists NFKBIE ENST00000275015 missense (canonical, protein_coding, TSL empty in the MAF), TMEM151B ENST00000451188 upstream_gene_variant, and NFKBIE ENST00000477930 upstream_gene_variant (no DISTANCE, TSL or biotype given in all_effects). These calls are not non-coding with respect to the canonical protein-coding isoform as annotated. However, Whiteside et al. 1997 (EMBO J) report that the first Met of the 500-aa IkBe ORF is in a poor Kozak context and translation starts at a second Met, giving a 45 kDa protein. So codon 34 is not translated in vivo and lies in functional 5' untranslated sequence about 100 bp from the TSS. I fixed my definition before deciding: a mutation in the untranslated 5' end or core-promoter region within about 1 kb of the TSS counts. Under it the label False holds, with the caveat that the variants are downstream of the annotated TSS.

label: LEARNED
text: LEARNED: The NFKBIE/IkBe 500-aa ORF's first methionine is in a poor translation context, and translation starts at a second downstream methionine (45 kDa protein), so the 5' part of the annotated canonical CDS (including codon 34, chr6:44233400) is effectively untranslated. USED FOR: deciding whether the c.101G>A hotspot counts as a 5' regulatory/promoter-region mutation. SOURCE: https://ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC1169738/

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (decision rule): I re-ran the pairing. 30 patients have both PRE-TX and POST-TX samples. 18 of them are trastuzumab-treated, ERBB2-amplified (cna==2) before treatment and had a CR/PR/SD best response. 2 of the 18 lost amplification (P-0000444, YJ-her-010); 3 POD pairs are excluded and none lost it. The 2/18 result (previously reported as 2/20) meets the pre-registered 'False' rule: at least 2 losses, one robust (YJ-her-010: same site, high purity, IHC 3+ to 0), and 0 losses in controls. The control arm is only 2 pairs, which is the weak point. The label is unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (alternative acquired alterations): Among the 18 acquired-resistance pairs, restricted to genes profiled in both samples, ERBB2 amplification loss (2/18) is among the most recurrent acquired events. KRAS has 3 events (2 mutations + 1 amplification), PIK3CA, JAK1 and SMAD4 have 2 mutations each, and MET and CCNE1 have 1 amplification each. Loss of CDK12 amplification (3) tracks the ERBB2 amplicon. ERBB2 loss is not rarer than the other candidate resistance mechanisms, so it is weighted no less. Method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (background discordance): Only 6 PRE/POST pairs did not receive trastuzumab (P-0000797, -1047, -1551, -1699, YJ-her-006, YJ-her-014), and only 2 of them were ERBB2-amplified. Neither lost ERBB2, and none of the 6 lost any amplified gene. Fisher's exact test for 2/18 vs 0/2 gives p=1.0. The internal control is far too small to give a background rate, so the 2 losses are not a statistically demonstrated excess over background. This weakens, but does not reverse, the evidence; the label is unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q4 (subclone marker vs outcome, not relying on 2 events): I took 54 trastuzumab-treated patients who were ERBB2-amplified in a PRE-TX sample and had a recorded HER2_RESPONSE, and split them at the median pre-TX HER2_IMPACT_LR. The lower-LR group, a proxy for a heterogeneous or partly non-amplified tumour that is confounded by purity, had shorter HER2_TTP_ON_1ST_LINE_MONTHS (median 9.9 vs 15.7 months, Mann-Whitney p=0.040) and fewer CR/PR (14/27 vs 22/27, Fisher p=0.042). Spearman correlation of LR with TTP was rho=0.29, p=0.03. IHC/FISH-negative vs HER2_IMPACT-amplified discordance (10 vs 44 patients) showed no TTP difference (p=0.53). No patient had discordant pre-TX regions. The test agrees with 'False' (association present) and does not change the method.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (panels): All 69 samples were run on MSK-IMPACT (341:3, 410:21, 468:45), with the same panel for mutations, CNA and SV. data_cna.txt has 1676 gene rows and includes YAP1, MYCL, MYC, MYCN, NKX2-1, SOX2, REST, NOTCH1, RB1 and TP53. ASCL1, NEUROD1 and POU2F3 appear in no file, and none of the 223 mutated Hugo symbols match them. Their absence is structural (never measured), not 'measured and unaltered'. This confirms Not verifiable; no method change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (histology/YAP1): The 42 PDX are Small Cell Lung Cancer/SCLC (40) and Combined SCLC/CSCLC (2). Histology does not separate SCLC-A/N/P. In data_cna.txt, YAP1 across the PDX is 0 in 39, -1 in 2 and +2 in 1. Copy number is not expression, and YAP1 does not define the A/N/P subtypes anyway. Per the library finding, no validated DNA mutation or CNA subtype proxy exists (only methylation, which is absent here). No histology or gene-level variable can serve as a proxy. No method change.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (CDX): Among the 42 SAMPLE_CLASS=PDX samples, PROCEDURE_TYPE is Biopsy 12, Autopsy 9, Blood Draw 8, Surgical 7, Aspiration 3 and Pleural Effusion 3. The 8 Blood Draw/blood xenografts are plausibly CTC-derived (CDX) models filed under PDX. Including or separating them does not change the variables searched: those samples have the same IMPACT tables and no expression, IHC or subtype field. No method change.

text: REPLY (segment filter): Dropping segments with num.mark<10 or <1 Mb removes 90-97% of segments in every sample. T-vs-first-X 1 Mb discordance then becomes threshold-sensitive: SA534 0.09-0.41, SA536 0.12-0.52, SA535 0.12-0.20, SA493 0.12-0.16, SA531 0.04-0.13, SA501 0.01-0.03. Baselines are SA429X2A/X5A 0.18-0.22 and SA501X1A/X5A 0.055. SA534 and SA536 exceed the SA429 baseline only at gain/loss thresholds of 0.2-0.3, not at 0.4. The method holds but the CNA evidence is weaker than first reported.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (7 first-passage pairs, WGS: SA493 X1, SA501 X1A, SA531 X1, SA533 X1, SA534 X1A, SA535 X1A, SA536 X0): mutation loss is 6.5-16% (SA493 15.6, SA533 16.2, SA536 13.8), which is within the X-X loss baseline of 13.6% (SA429) and 24% (SA501). Against the conservative SA429 CNA baseline at most 2 of 7 (SA534, SA536) exceed, and not robustly. Against SA501X1A/X5A, 4-5 of 7 exceed. The label therefore rests on the CNA evidence at first passage measured against the tighter baseline, not on SA494/SA500; it is weak.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (baseline): No same-passage WGS replicates exist. Splitting SA501X1A vs X5A by chromosome (filtered, recentred) gives 0 chromosomes with >50% discordant bins and a median of 0.01; SA429X2A/X5A gives 3-5 chromosomes and a median of 0.08-0.11. First-passage T-X: SA534 9/6/0 and SA536 10/4/3 chromosomes at thresholds 0.2/0.3/0.4; SA493 2-3; SA535 2; SA533 0-2; SA531 0-1; SA501 0. Only SA534 and SA536 clearly exceed the SA429 level, and both have low-purity T (rescale k 2.3-2.6), which amplifies noise.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY (lost mutations): t_alt_count, t_ref_count and dbSNP_RS are empty in all rows (0 non-empty). Across 9 T-vs-X pairs the T-only WGS calls are 34% RNA, 26% missense, 16% intron and 11% silent; MA:FImpact is mostly NA, with only 4 high. Most lie in segments that are not lost in X: for example SA533 31/70 in X cn<-0.3, which matches the 32% of shared mutations there. So mutation loss is weak, noise-level evidence and does not by itself show selection.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (chr21 deletion proxy): In data_cna_hg19.seg, the length-weighted mean seg.mean over chr21:40.2-42.7 Mb (between ERG and TMPRSS2, hg19) was below -0.2 in 11 of 12 FISH 'Translocation with deletion' samples, 0 of 11 'Translocation' samples, 0 of 3 ERG-fusion samples without FISH and 1 of 31 fusion-negative samples (ERG-fusion vs none, Fisher p=5e-6). The proxy works, but it shows only how each fusion formed (interstitial deletion vs balanced), not whether rearrangements are interdependent chains. Method unchanged: Not verifiable.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (ERG_FISH_RESULT): In data_clinical_sample.txt, ERG_FISH_RESULT is 'Translocation with deletion' for 12 samples and 'Translocation' for 11; all 23 also have an ERG fusion in data_sv.txt. 11 of the 12 deletion cases are out-of-frame TMPRSS2-ERG. All non-TMPRSS2 or unusual fusions fall in 'Translocation': 2 SLC45A3-ERG, 1 ERG-TMPRSS2 and 1 antisense. This variable is relevant to fusion mechanism, so my earlier wording 'no relevant variables' was too strong. It is still per-fusion and cannot show multi-partner chained, interdependent rearrangements (library finding: FISH cannot show chromoplexy). Label unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (dysregulation part): Of 56 samples in data_cna.txt, these have GISTIC deep deletions (-2): PTEN 7, NKX3-1 7, CHD1 5, RB1 5, FOXP1 5, ZNF292 4, TMPRSS2 4, CDKN1B 2, TP53 1. All 28 SV fusions (26 ERG, 1 ETV1, 1 BRAF) have RNA_Support=Yes. So the data show that fusions and deletions often hit prostate cancer genes. They cannot attribute those events to chromoplexy rather than independent events, because there are no junctions or chains. Method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q1 (component table): chains of interdependent translocations/deletions -> none (data_sv.txt has 28 curated Fusion rows, gene names only, no coordinates/strands; seg gives CN segments without junction partners); dysregulation of prostate cancer genes -> partly (data_sv ERG/ETV1/BRAF fusions, ERG_FISH_RESULT, ETS_FUSION_SEQ, data_cna, mutations); frequency of chromoplexy -> none (needs chain calls). Only the gene-dysregulation component is testable, and only without linking it to chromoplexy; since the hypothesis's claim is that chromoplexy causes the dysregulation, the linking variable is absent. Method unchanged: Not verifiable.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q2 (seg breakpoints near prostate genes): in 57 WGS seg samples, deletion (seg.mean<-0.2) breakpoints within 1 Mb of 14 prostate genes/fusion partners number 605 vs 197 expected when gene windows are placed at random on the same chromosomes (p<0.002, 500 perms); 31 samples have such breakpoints on >=2 chromosomes. This shows recurrent focal deletions at known prostate cancer loci, but CN segments cannot say whether breakpoints on different chromosomes are joined, so it is not specific to chromoplexy. Seg file stays a weak proxy; method unchanged.

label: REPLY
text: REPLY Q3 (ERG FISH mechanism): ERG_FISH_RESULT vs SV ERG fusion: Translocation 11/11 and Translocation-with-deletion 12/12 have an SV ERG fusion. Seg chr21 ERG-TMPRSS2 interval mean log2 <-0.15 in 11/12 'with deletion' vs 1/11 'Translocation' (means -0.56 vs +0.02), so the FISH field matches the CN data. It shows how each ERG fusion formed (interstitial deletion vs copy-neutral rearrangement) but cannot show whether the copy-neutral ones are part of multi-chromosome chains. Method unchanged.

label: REFEREE TEST
text: Referee test on bd27 (NFKBIE promoter mutations in desmoplastic melanoma): the recurrent chr6:44233400 C>T is in 4/20 DM. The canonical annotation calls it G34E missense, but the transcript has no annotated 5'UTR (cDNA_pos == CDS_pos). 5 of 6 non-silent NFKBIE hits fall in the first 101 nt (binomial p~1e-5), so it is a 5' promoter-region hotspot. Picked the False label (Y).

label: REFEREE TEST
text: Referee test on DLBCL Duke (618 patients, 185 deaths): with the 3-level genomic PROGNOSTIC_MODEL compared with 3-group IPI (0-1/2-3/4-5) at equal df, the genomic model wins on AIC (2082 vs 2125) and C (0.673 vs 0.664). In a joint Cox model it adds LR chi2 96 vs 52 for IPI, and its loglik is higher in 95% of bootstraps. Full 0-5 IPI C of 0.682 is only non-significantly higher. Picked the True side; the advantage is in-sample.

label: REFEREE TEST
text: Referee test (NPC ERBB-PI3K, 56 exomes) using a length-weighted per-sample null: narrow ERBB+PI3K/PTEN/AKT gives p=0.06; ERBB+PI3K/AKT/mTOR with 20 genes gives 7/56 hit vs 2.5 expected, p=0.009; +RAS gives p=0.003; a KEGG ErbB-style 46-gene set fixed in advance gives p=0.038. Picked Y (label False): the pathway is significantly mutated under standard definitions.
